title: Synthetic history seeder (7 cohorts, is_demo household only, ENABLE_SEED gate)
goal: Build a deterministic synthetic-purchase-history generator (working spec Sec12) that seeds ~70 catalog items across the 7 documented cohorts into a dedicated is_demo household, each item carrying known ground-truth cadence/interval metadata that S-18's validator scores predictions against -- without ever touching the real DEFAULT_HOUSEHOLD_ID household.
in_scope: scripts/seed-history/plan.ts: pure, deterministic (seeded mulberry32 PRNG, fixed seed). generateItemDefs() returns ~70 ItemDef records (canonical_name, cohort, category_slug, base_unit, pack_size, perishability_days, is_staple, plus ground-truth generation params: target bucket, target interval days or a linear drift range, jitter sigma, purchase count, outlier injection point/direction, qty-missing fraction). generatePurchaseEvents(itemDef, anchorNowIso) is a separate pure function producing {occurredAt, qtyBase}[] walking backward from anchorNowIso, seeded per-item off the global seed so the sequence is reproducible -- called once by the seeder at seed time with the real now, never re-derived by the validator (S-18 reads actual stock_movements back from the DB instead of regenerating timestamps, so the two scripts never need matching RNG state at different invocation times).

7 cohorts per working spec Sec12's table, ~70 items total: clean_periodic (25, sigma=0.15, spread across all 8 non-unpredictable cadence buckets -- daily/every_2_3_days/weekly/fortnightly/monthly/quarterly/half_yearly/yearly -- weighted toward buckets that can reach n>=4 purchases inside computeItemStats' own 24-month lookback: 3/3/4/4/4/4/2/1), high_variance (10, sigma=0.40, weekly/fortnightly/monthly targets only, enough n to isolate variance from data-starvation), outlier_injected (8, sigma=0.15 baseline with exactly one interval multiplied ~3.2x or reduced to ~0.3x injected mid-sequence, weekly/fortnightly targets, >=8 purchases so the post-rejection n stays >=4), drifting (8, true interval linearly interpolated 7d->14d oldest-to-newest across the seeded window, category prior chosen near the drift midpoint (~10-12d) per the resolved deviation below), cold_start (10, split ~3/3/4 across exactly 1/2/3 total purchases each, no held-out testing possible -- informational only), perishable_implausible_rate (5, true interval ~30d with a large pack size so the rate cross-check would compute a depletion date far beyond a short perishability_days override, testing the clamp), qty_inconsistent (4, weekly/fortnightly target with ~50% of events carrying qtyBase=null so q<0.70).

Category assignment picks the closest-prior seeded leaf category to each item's target interval (from the existing ~60 S-02 categories, e.g. milk/prior=2 for daily-target items, first-aid/prior=90 for quarterly-target items) so shrinkage isn't fighting an arbitrarily mismatched prior at low n -- this is a deliberate, documented cohort-design choice, not tuning the algorithm itself.

scripts/seed-history.ts: entry point (npm run seed:history, optionally `-- --wipe`). Manually parses .env.local (no new dependency; strips \r for Windows CRLF safety) for SUPABASE_URL/SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY/DEFAULT_HOUSEHOLD_ID, gated on ENABLE_SEED=true (refuses to run otherwise). Constructs its own @supabase/supabase-js client directly -- never imports lib/supabase/server.ts, which throws under plain tsx via the 'server-only' package's react-server export condition.

Write guard (working spec Sec12's 'writes only to a household flagged is_demo=true' contract, treated as load-bearing): before any insert or delete, re-read the target household row by its fixed DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID constant and assert both is_demo===true and id !== DEFAULT_HOUSEHOLD_ID; refuse (throw, no writes) otherwise. Applied identically on the seed path and the --wipe path.

Idempotent reseed: on a normal (non-wipe) run, first deletes all existing rows scoped to DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID (item_stats_history, item_stats, stock_movements, item_aliases, catalog_items, in FK-safe order) through the same guarded delete path as --wipe, then upserts the demo household row (is_demo=true, stock_epoch backdated before the earliest seeded movement so v_current_stock resolves correctly for demo items), inserts catalog_items, re-reads them by canonical_name to get ids, generates purchase events per item, and inserts stock_movements (type='purchase', source_receipt_id null, chunked ~500 rows/batch).
--wipe mode: runs only the guarded delete path (household row itself is left in place, so a later plain `npm run seed:history` reseeds cleanly) and prints a summary.

package.json: add `tsx` as an explicit devDependency (was previously resolved ad hoc via npx's on-demand fetch, not in package-lock.json -- fragile for a now-permanent script) and two scripts, `seed:history` and `validate:predictions` (S-18).
out_of_scope: Any change to lib/predictions/computeItemStats.ts (S-18's territory, only if a genuine defect is found and re-verified against E-5's fixtures).

Persisting item_stats/item_stats_history rows for demo items -- the validator (S-18) calls computeItemStats directly in-memory; the demo household is never touched by the nightly cron (app/api/cron/recompute-stats/route.ts always targets getDefaultHouseholdId()) or by recomputeOneItem/recomputeAllItemsForHousehold, so there is no reason for this story to write item_stats at all.

A UI affordance for triggering seed/wipe -- CLI-only, matches the working spec's `pnpm seed:history` framing (renamed to `npm run seed:history` to match this repo's actual package manager, see ledger).
acceptance: `npm run seed:history` (ENABLE_SEED=true gate) generates ~70 catalog items across the 7 documented cohorts under a dedicated is_demo household, each with known ground-truth cadence/interval metadata, spanning up to 24 months of purchase history (bounded by computeItemStats' own step-1 lookback window, not a literal fixed 12 months -- see ledger for why); `npm run seed:history -- --wipe` removes all of that household's data in one command; every write path is guarded to refuse touching any household that isn't the fixed demo id with is_demo=true.
invariants: Never writes to DEFAULT_HOUSEHOLD_ID or any household other than the fixed DEMO_HOUSEHOLD_ID constant -- enforced by the write guard on every insert/delete call, not just checked once at startup.

generateItemDefs() is pure and deterministic (fixed PRNG seed) -- re-running it (e.g. from S-18's validator) always produces the same 70 canonical_name/cohort/ground-truth records in the same order, with no DB dependency.

The demo household is invisible to every production code path that matters: the nightly cron is hardcoded to getDefaultHouseholdId() (app/api/cron/recompute-stats/route.ts), and the on-commit trigger (lib/review/commit.ts) only ever fires for a real committed receipt -- this story writes stock_movements directly, never through the receipt/commit pipeline, so on-commit recompute never runs for demo items either. Seeding a second household cannot corrupt the real household's Today/Inventory/Plan screens or its item_stats.
